# Spec-pack — the single contract every input adapter must emit

> **Phase 2 packet (ingest).** Read it first, then read exactly **one** `from-*.md` that matches what you were given. From Phase 3
> on, everything reads the spec-pack and **never** goes back to the original source.

## Why it exists

A running Joomla site, an HTML folder, a live URL, a brief — they have nothing in common
structurally. Instead of teaching the pipeline four source formats, each input has a **thin adapter** that emits the same set of
files. The pipeline is blind to the input.

```
INPUT              ADAPTER                          SPEC-PACK               PIPELINE
Joomla (j6-dir) →  scripts/ingest/from-joomla.mjs ┐  page-map.json        ┐  P3 chrome
HTML bundle/dir →  scripts/ingest/from-html.mjs   │  design-spec.md       │  P4 theme.json
live URL        →  scripts/ingest/from-url.mjs    ├→ design-contract.json ├→ P5 template + pattern
brief           →  hand-written                   ┘  content-contract.json│  P6 css/dark · P7 content
                                                     reference/ + .json   │  P8 verify · P8b review
                                                     provenance.json      ┘  P9 package · P10 quickstart
```

**The adapter is the ONLY place that knows the source format.** If Phase 5 has to reopen `inventory.json` or the URL, the
adapter extracted too little — go back and fix the spec-pack, do not patch in place.

## Layout

Write it **outside** the WordPress webroot so it never ends up in the package (Tracy Base run: `tasks/tracy-base-wp7/spec/`):

```
<spec>/
  page-map.json          # theme identity, palette, fonts, pages[], templateParts, menus, gaps
  design-spec.md         # design system as text + tables; generated by make-design-spec.mjs, then fill every slot
  design-contract.json   # MEASURED type/colour/spacing roles, 4 variants, coverage, exceptions with reasons
  content-contract.json  # facts about the site: facts, sources, voice, demo|customer, one surface per page
  reference/             # comparison target per page (per reference.json)
  reference.json         # kind · viewports · modes · pages[]
  assets/                # images/fonts pulled from the source (from-joomla does NOT copy images — see from-joomla.md)
  provenance.json        # adapter, source, time, notes[] — every decision the adapter made on its own
  source-fonts.json      # source font evidence; Joomla uses the Joomla report, HTML/URL use the DOM report
  content.json           # site content, pages, posts, categories, archives — payload for the seeder
  sections.json          # section instances; menus.json — navigation; redirects.json — redirects
```

The `from-html` and `from-url` adapters write `source-fonts.json`: the static CSS of every reference page (families by
role when the CSS declares them, `@font-face`, font sources, loaders, and missing/unreadable stylesheets) plus the browser
measurement when `--render` is run. The Phase 2 gate applies the same way to both static reports. A DOM pack without the
browser part must be rebuilt with `--render`; the gate requires every reference page at 1440 and 390 px.
A `source-font` finding can only be waived by a closed decision in `DECISIONS.md` that names the exact key.

Every adapter writes four payloads for the seeder (`content.json` · `sections.json` · `menus.json` ·
`redirects.json`): `from-joomla`, `from-html` and `from-brief` write them directly; `from-url` uses the pipeline
of `from-html`. The validator requires all four files and checks the JSON and the top-level shape the seeder reads. This
is part of a seedable spec-pack; the check does not replace each adapter's own deep schema.

Optional `content.json` fields any adapter may write, each checked by the seeder (demo-content.md §6c):
`posts[].meta._wp_page_template` (a post rendered through a template of its own, still a post — the theme must
declare it for posts, `customTemplates[].postTypes` containing `"post"`); `posts[].meta.<key>` (text post meta
for Block Bindings: a lower-case key, not `_…`, not `tracy_…`; a string, number or boolean);
`posts[].route` `{ path, contentKind, content, aside?, modules? }` (the modules of the menu route that opens the post, around
its body marker);
`authors[]` `{ id, name, login?, description?, avatar?, avatarAlt? }` with `posts[].author.id` pointing at one
(a source identity, so a rename is the same user and two people of one name stay two); `archives[].perPage`
(a positive integer; cards per page, with a pager) with `archives[].paging.links` (link-only titles after
the cards, a count ≥ 0) and `archives[].moreArticles` `{ heading }` (the text over them). A page-map `single` page may name its article with
`source.articleId`; the seeder then points that path at that post and no other. Absent, each keeps the old
behaviour.

One **hand-written** file may sit beside them: `copy.json` — `{ "fixes": [{ "find", "replace",
"reason" }] }`, text where the site says something different from the design (the 404 copy says "on the right" while at 390 the suggestion block
sits below; a Title Case heading in a sentence-case list). `seed.mjs` applies it when loading the spec to every
string of the four files above (both `html` and `fields`, so pattern coverage does not change), matching literally and
case-sensitively; `find` must carry enough of the sentence not to hit a file name ("Corporate Deck 2028 — full slide
library", not "Corporate Deck 2028" — which is also the name of a PDF). Adapters do not overwrite it on
`--force`, so a re-ingest does not lose it; a fix that hits nothing is recorded in the report's `notes` — the text it
meant to fix has moved.

## 1. `page-map.json` — WordPress vocabulary

```jsonc
{
  "template": { "name": "tracy-base", "title": "Tracy Base" },   // name = theme slug = text domain = folder name
  "theme": {
    "palette": { "light": { "primary": "#0071e3", "secondary": "…", "body_bg": "…", "text": "…" }, "dark": { … } },
    "darkDerived": false,                                        // true ONLY when palette.dark is null
    "fonts": { "body": "SF Pro Text", "heading": "SF Pro Display" }
  },
  "scope": { "mode": "template" },                               // website | template | edit
  "templateParts": ["header", "footer"],
  "pages": [ { "file": "index.html", "view": "front-page", "path": "/", "sections": [ … ] }, … ],
  "menus": [ … ], "gaps": [ … ],
  "reference": "reference.json", "provenance": "provenance.json"
}
```

**`view` is a WordPress template name**, not a Joomla view. The validator (`scripts/ingest/spec-pack.mjs`,
`WP_TEMPLATES` · `WP_TEMPLATE_PARTS` · `PAGE_TEMPLATE_RE`) only accepts:

| Group | Valid values |
|---|---|
| Template hierarchy | `front-page` `page` `single` `home` `archive` `category` `tag` `author` `date` `search` `404` |
| Custom page template | `page-<name>` (`^page-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`): `page-landing`, `page-onepage`, `page-contact`, `page-login`… — each must have `templates/<name>.html` and a `customTemplates` row |
| Template part | `header` `footer` |

**Pages are required for six views** (`REQUIRED_VIEWS`): `front-page` · `page` · `single` · `category` ·
`search` · `404`. If the source has no route for `single`/`404`, the adapter **adds a synthetic page**
(`synthetic: true`) — `from-joomla` does exactly that. Check the names against
[`../wordpress-anatomy.md`](../wordpress-anatomy.md) §2 (template hierarchy).

The validator checks on `page-map.json`:

- `template.name` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` (WordPress theme slug); `template.title` is not empty.
- `theme.palette.light` has all **four** cells `primary` `secondary` `body_bg` `text`, each a parseable CSS colour
  (hex, `rgb()/hsl()/oklch()/color()…`, or a real CSS colour name — an unknown word is a placeholder, not a colour).
- `theme.palette.dark`: either all four cells, or `null` **together with** `theme.darkDerived: true`. Declaring both is an error.
  The intent must be **data**, not a sentence in `design-spec.md` — the T4 version used to read prose and a
  sentence saying "do not derive" also passed.
- `theme.fonts.body` is not empty.
- `scope.mode` ∈ `website | template | edit`; other than `template`, `scope.reason` is required and `scope.pages`
  must match `pages[].file` **exactly**.
- `pages[]` ≥ floor (`PAGE_FLOOR` = 12 in `template` mode, 1 in the other two modes); `--page-floor N` changes the floor.
- No two pages with the same `file` (N copies of one page do not count toward the floor).
- Every `pages[].file` has a `surfaces[].id` in `content-contract.json` and a `pages[].id` in
  `design-contract.json`.

## 2. `design-spec.md`

The design system as prose + tables: token names, light/dark palette, type scale, spacing scale, class prefix,
**dark hook**, and **a source pointer for each artifact** (which URL / selector /
module each chrome part / section comes from). Generate the skeleton with `scripts/make-design-spec.mjs <page-map.json> --out <spec>/design-spec.md`,
then fill **every** `` `TODO` `` slot (in backticks — the validator matches exactly that mark, not the word TODO
in an instruction sentence). For a source slot that is not declared, write "not declared in the source" outright — do not invent numbers.

**Theme name** (product decision): a JoomlArt source named "JA <Name>" is ported as "WP <Name>" — the `Theme Name` in `style.css`, the `readme.txt` title and the pattern category label. `generate-docs.mjs --check` enforces it for `wp-ja-*` slugs. Folder, slug, text domain, quickstart card label, release title, `blogname` and any text naming the source template or the JoomlArt product stay as they are.

`from-joomla` fills the slots from `etc/site/*.json` + the template's CSS tokens; the other adapters leave the slots for
a person to fill.

## 3. `reference.json` — the only thing Phase 8 branches on

```jsonc
{
  "kind": "url",
  "viewports": [1440, 390],
  "modes": ["light", "dark"],
  "pages": [
    { "page": "index.html", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8217/" },
    { "page": "landing.html", "kind": "image", "shots": { "light": "reference/landing-light.png", "dark": "…" } }
  ]
}
```

| `kind` | Emitted by adapter | What Phase 8 does |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | `from-html` · `from-url` | Phase 8 compares against captured HTML files. For URL captures, provenance records adapter `from-url` and source kind `url`. |
| `url` | `from-joomla` | Phase 8 compares against the live URL. Provenance records source kind `url`. |
| `image` | (no adapter yet — see `from-pen.md`, `from-figma.md`) | Compares images per viewport/mode **and** asserts the measurements against the tables in `design-spec.md`. |
| `none` | `from-brief` | No external target. Every source comparison has a typed not-applicable tied to the spec; the sweep still measures target-side invariants, a round always runs the sweep, release requires complete, verified evidence. A target-side error or a missing measurement still blocks release. |

Validator rules:

- The package-level `kind` is the default; a page-level `kind` overrides it. But a page **may not** declare `none` when the package
  is not `none` — that is how a package "passes" with 0 targets checked.
- `path` / `shots` are **relative to the spec-pack root** and **must not escape it** (resolve, then compare the prefix).
  A missing or **empty** file is an error — Phase 8 would silently skip that page and report pass.
- `url` must be `http(s)://`.
- `viewports` must have at least one mobile width (≤ 430) and one desktop width (≥ 1280).
- `modes` must have both `light` and `dark`, unless `theme.darkDerived: true`.
- Every `pages[].file` of the page-map has a `pages[].page` row (except for a `none` package).

The OK line prints the number of targets **actually checked**: `spec-pack OK — 40 pages, kind=url, 40 reference target(s) checked,
adapter=from-joomla`. When that number is 0, the package has nothing to compare against, even though it is "OK".

## 4. `assets/`

Images, SVGs, fonts pulled from the source, keeping the original names when possible. Phase 6b copies them into the theme (`assets/images/`) or the
media library. **Licence discipline:** record each asset's source in `provenance.json`; assets scraped from someone
else's site are placeholders and must be replaced before Phase 9. `from-joomla` **does not copy images** — it only changes `src` to
`/wp-content/uploads/<basename>` and lists them; the seeder uploads them itself from the original `images/` tree.

**Image table contract.** An uploads-style `src` carries only the file name; the identity is the `{ src, file, original, alt }` entry
in the `images[]` table of **the very** page / post / section that mentions it (`original` = the path in the `images/` tree;
inline images in a list item add `width`/`height`). The seeder resolves names through that table first (demo-content.md §4), so
an adapter must list every image it writes into markup in the table of the markup's owner, **with `original`**: an entry without a source
path is not resolved (the seeder does not guess by name across the whole site). Two different source files with the same name
in **one** table cannot be told apart by the seeder: `src` stays as is and the report says so — any adapter that meets that
case should give the files different names.

## 5. `provenance.json`

```jsonc
{ "adapter": "from-joomla", "adapterVersion": "1.0",
  "source": { "kind": "joomla", "dir": "…/tracy-base-j6-1.0.0", "siteUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8217" },
  "generatedAt": "2026-09-13T…Z", "tools": { "node": "v24.11.1" },
  "counts": { … }, "notes": [ "synthetic pages added for required views with no route: single.html, 404.html", … ] }
```

The validator requires `adapter`, `source`, `generatedAt`. `notes[]` answers "where did this number come from" three weeks later.

**Paths in kept records** (`provenance.json`, `content-contract.json` `sources.*.reference`,
`adapter-coverage.json`, `page-map.json` `source`, `attempts/superseded-*/SUPERSEDED.json`, the release's `VERIFICATION.json`,
`run-record.mjs` notes) do not record one machine's layout. Tools write them through
`scripts/lib/record-paths.mjs`: a path inside the repository that holds the record → relative to the repository root
(`tasks/<site>/design-contract.json`); outside it, under the home folder → `~/…` (`~/tracy-data/<site>/j6`); anything else
stays as is. A run's artifact/scratch folder or a runner's state folder names both the machine and the run,
so it may not be recorded even as `~/…`: declare it as a **named root** — the tool passes `roots: [{ name, dir }]`, or set
`TRACY_RECORD_ROOTS=artifacts=/path/to/dir` (several entries joined by the PATH separator) — and the record says `<artifacts>/…`.
Relative command-line arguments are made absolute before recording, so the record does not depend on the current folder. Tools still use absolute paths when opening files and calling child processes — only the representation at record time changes.
When reading back, use `resolveRecordPath`: it accepts both new forms and the absolute paths that older tool versions wrote.

## Gate — run before Phase 3

```bash
node scripts/ingest/spec-pack.mjs --validate <spec> [--page-floor N]
```

Exits non-zero and prints **one line per error**; it checks the **required files first** (`page-map.json`, `design-spec.md`,
`reference.json`, `provenance.json`, `content-contract.json`, `design-contract.json` and the four seeder payloads
`content.json`, `sections.json`, `menus.json`, `redirects.json`)
and stops there, so the first run on a new package usually only shows "missing required file". Add whatever is missing
and rerun — the deep checks (page floor, required views, slots, targets) only show up then.

**Nothing downstream may read a spec-pack that has not passed the gate.** The checks are deliberately crude: missing fields, dangling
paths, unfilled slots, page count below the floor — exactly the errors that lie dormant until Phase 8 and then cost a rebuild.

`--init <dir> --page-map <file> [--kind …] [--adapter …] [--force]` builds the skeleton (page-map + reference +
provenance + two empty contracts with `pending`); it **refuses to overwrite** an existing package without `--force`, because
rerunning the adapter would wipe the hand-filled palette/`sections[]`/images. `--force` keeps the two existing
contracts.

## Choosing an adapter

| Given | Read | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A Joomla quickstart folder (`inventory.json` + `render-routes.json` + `capture/templates/<tpl>`) | [`from-joomla.md`](from-joomla.md) | **proven** on Tracy Base j6 (40 pages, 51 posts, 14 categories, 3 menus, 46 ACM) |
| An HTML folder (a bundle with `manifest.json`, or a raw `.html` folder) | [`from-html.md`](from-html.md) | ported from T4, so far proven only by tests |
| A live site URL | [`from-url.md`](from-url.md) | ported from T4, so far proven only by tests |
| A brief / topic, no design | [`from-brief.md`](from-brief.md) | hand-written |
| Pencil `.pen` · Figma | [`from-pen.md`](from-pen.md) · [`from-figma.md`](from-figma.md) | **no adapter yet** |

With two sources at once (a live Joomla site **and** a sample URL), choose **one** as the design authority, build the
spec-pack from it, and record the other in `provenance.json.notes`. Do not mix two adapters — a mixed authority is how
a port ends up matching no source.
